messages:
ella (customer): Hey — trying to redeem promo code SPRINGBOOST on my account (ella@example.com). Dashboard shows it as active with 5 left, but checkout API returns 422 'invalid_or_expired'. Can someone check?

jamie (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error you saw (response body) and the time you tried?

ella (customer): Sure. Tried at 2024-04-08T16:12:04Z. API response: 422 Unprocessable Entity
{"error":"promo_invalid_or_expired","details":{"reason":"invalid_scope","allowed_countries":["GB","IE"]}}

jamie (support): Thanks. That looks like the code is scoped to GB/IE. But you said dashboard shows 'global' and 5 redemptions left?

ella (customer): Yep — dashboard UI (promo config page) shows Region: Any, Remaining: 5. I attached a screenshot but here is the promo id from the admin URL: promo_98765

jamie (support): I'm going to pull the backend logs and escalate if the services disagree. Give me ~10 min.

jamie (support): Quick findings: our promo-api call to rules-service returned country-block for CA (country code from your IP). rules-service responded with rule set that only contains GB/IE. However the promo record in billing DB has region='ALL'. This smells like a config propagation problem between the UI/config store and the rules-service cached snapshot. Escalating to eng.

alex (billing): Looking at promo_98765 in billing-db:
- status: active
- remaining_redemptions: 5
- start: 2024-03-01T00:00:00Z
- end: 2024-05-01T00:00:00Z
No per-country block in billing row. Admin UI change log shows admin 'maria' removed a country filter at 2024-04-07T22:05:12Z.

jamie (support): So DB + UI agree, rules-service disagrees. Tim from eng taking over.

tim (eng): I pulled rules-service sync logs. Last successful config sync for campaign rules was 2024-04-07T21:58:03Z. There was a retry loop at 22:05 while the UI change was committed; our config-push to S3 returned a 204 but the rules-service S3 client encountered a 404 on the object for ~90s due to eventual consistency in the S3 region (edge case). It then fell back to an older snapshot (which still had the GB/IE filter). Log excerpt: 
`WARN rules-sync - promo_98765: config fetch failed (404) after push, falling back to snapshot v20240407-2158`

tim (eng): Repro steps if you want to see the mismatch locally:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promo/apply -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"promo_code":"SPRINGBOOST","account_email":"ella@example.com","country":"CA"}'
2) Response when rules-service outdated: 422 with the invalid_scope body (allowed_countries: ["GB","IE"])
3) After forcing config-sync (see below), same request returns 200 and credit applied.

tim (eng): Short-term mitigation: I triggered a manual config-sync job on rules-service and invalidated the local cache for promo_98765. That should propagate in ~30s. Long-term fix: we'll add a stronger confirmation/backoff after failed fetches and surface failed syncs to the console (ENG-2304).

config-sync-bot: Manual config sync triggered by tim at 2024-04-08T16:38:12Z. Status: success.

jamie (support): @ella can you try the promo again? If it still fails I can grant a manual one-off credit to unblock you and we'll follow up once eng completes the postmortem.

ella (customer): Re-tried at 2024-04-08T16:39:05Z — worked! Thanks for the quick help. Applied 1,000 credits. :party_parrot:

jamie (support): Great — leaving this thread open until ENG posts the follow-up. Action items:
- tim: create ENG-2304 PR to improve sync robustness and alerting (assigned)
- alex: confirm the admin UI shows the sync status to ops (follow-up)
- jamie: email customer that promo applied and include manual-credit fallback details

tim (eng): Will add a small sanity check: if DB and rules-service disagree on region, auto-trigger a sync and return a transient 503 instead of a hard 422 until sync completes.

jamie (support): Closing for now since customer is unblocked — marking as resolved but will reopen if any postmortem actions reveal further risk. :thumbsup:
